input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

## Meeting notes

The meeting was held on May 14 in the small meeting room at Morrow Street Library. Present were Leonie Ward, Ellis Grant, facilities volunteer Omar Bell, and branch coordinator Priya Shah. The group met because visitors and staff had raised several repair issues over the previous two months. No contractor attended. Priya recorded the notes. The figures discussed were rough volunteer estimates, not quotes. The library is open Tuesday through Saturday. The meeting did not set work dates or decide whether repairs would take place while the building is open.

### Front entrance
The front entrance door sticks when it is damp, and the lower hinge looks loose. Omar said he can tighten the hinge and check whether the door still catches, but he cannot promise that adjustment will solve the problem. A replacement closer was discussed as a possibility. Volunteers estimated $180 to $240 for parts and installation if a contractor is needed. Nobody confirmed that the closer is the cause. The group wants the entrance to remain usable throughout repairs. There is a side entrance, but it is not step-free and should not be treated as an equivalent route for every visitor.

### Children's room ceiling
Two ceiling tiles in the children's room have brown marks after rain. Priya said the marks were dry at the time of the meeting. No one inspected the roof or established whether the tiles or roof are currently leaking. The group discussed asking the property manager to inspect the roof before replacing the tiles. Volunteers may be able to help move chairs and shelves if the tiles are replaced, but they have not been asked to do work above the ceiling. A replacement tile was estimated at $18 each. That estimate does not cover finding or repairing a possible roof leak. Do not describe a leak as confirmed.

### West wall paint
A section of paint roughly four feet across is peeling on the west wall near the radiator. Ellis thinks the paint may have lifted because the radiator gets hot, but this is a guess, not a finding. Omar offered to scrape and repaint the small area if the library can get matching paint. The old paint can is in the locked supply closet, and Priya has the key. No one knows whether its color label is still readable. One volunteer estimated $45 for paint and basic supplies if a new can is needed. The radiator was not tested, and the notes do not say it needs repair.

### Reading-room chairs
Three reading-room chairs are loose: one wobbles at a rear leg, one has a split seat board, and one has a loose armrest. Omar can inspect the joints on Saturday but has not agreed to repair all three. The meeting estimate for replacement parts was $30 to $75 total, depending on what can be tightened instead of replaced. The group does not want the chairs returned to use until someone checks that they are stable. There are currently 18 other chairs in the reading room; the notes do not say whether that is enough during busy hours.

### Accessible restroom faucet
The accessible restroom faucet drips slowly at the handle. Priya has logged the issue with the property manager but has received no reply. Leonie offered to call again on Monday if there is still no response. Nobody agreed to let a volunteer take the faucet apart. Omar estimated that a replacement washer might cost about $8, but he did not inspect the faucet and said the actual part could differ. The restroom remains available; the group did not discuss closing it or posting a sign.

### Funds and availability
The meeting listed $600 as the amount currently available in the small repairs fund. Priya checked that figure against the library group's notebook, but nobody checked it against a bank statement. The amount is not approval to spend. The possible amounts above are individual rough estimates and may not include labor, delivery, or tax. The group has not approved a contractor, ordered materials, assigned a full budget, or decided which repair should come first. Omar can usually volunteer on Saturdays. Leonie said she may be available after 4 p.m. on Mondays; neither person's availability is a confirmed work appointment.

### Discussion for the next meeting
Priya said, “Let’s separate what we saw from what we’re guessing, so the next meeting can decide what to do.” The group wants its next discussion to cover which items need a professional inspection, what volunteers can do, and which costs still need checking. These notes do not give a date for the next meeting.

Prepare the repair plan from these notes. Include the fund amount while making clear that it is not spending authorization, and keep all estimates qualified as estimates. Note the front-entrance access concern and the uncertainty about a possible roof leak. End with the unresolved decisions and information the group wants to discuss next, without deciding those matters for the group."}]
